No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) are triggered by the provided full text. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal using static IAPS images in healthy adult participants and reports group-level peak coordinates, the paper’s primary reported results are between-group comparisons (high-Mach vs low-Mach) rather than within-task regulation contrasts for the target sample (e.g., reappraise > look or down-regulate > maintain) across the whole healthy sample. I therefore apply exclusion E7 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (reappraisal/reinterpretation used), I7 (static visual IAPS stimuli), I8 (healthy adult sample), I10 (group-level coordinates reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I9 (no clear within-task emotion-regulation contrast for the target sample reported in the provided full text). Full text appears complete for the main article (supplementary analyses are referenced but not provided here).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=59) that used cognitive reappraisal (increase/decrease) as the emotion regulation strategy. The experiment included static visual images (IAPS pictures) and the authors report within-task contrasts (Increase>Look; Decrease>Look; Increase>Decrease) analyzed separately for IAPS and film clips. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates are reported in multiple tables (univariate contrasts and conjunctions), satisfying whole-brain coordinate reporting. Although the study also included film clips, the presence of separate analyses and reported coordinates for the IAPS (static image) condition means it meets the review requirement that regulated stimuli are static visual images. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text provided, and no exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, patient-only) are violated.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study using reappraisal (distancing) of static IAPS images and includes a healthy control group, the full text reports only between-group whole-brain contrasts (marijuana users > controls) with peak coordinates. The paper does not present group-level, whole-brain reappraisal activation coordinates specifically for the healthy control group (i.e., within-task 'reappraise>look' or equivalent contrast for controls) required by the meta-analysis. Thus it fails inclusion criteria I9 and I10 and meets exclusion criterion E7 (reports only between-group contrasts). Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not include a healthy adult sample reported separately (Inclusion criterion I8 not met). It otherwise meets task and analysis requirements: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (cognitive reappraisal employed), I7 (static visual images—IAPS), I9 (reports within-task contrast Reappraise > Look-Negative), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with MNI peak coordinates), and I11 (results clearly described/tabled). No exclusion criteria from the review (E4–E8) are triggered by the full text. Therefore exclusion is solely due to failure to meet I8 (no healthy control group whose results are reported separately). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructed participants to use cognitive reappraisal to downregulate emotion (meets I5,I6). Stimuli were static images (neutral, fearful, and OCD-related pictures) (I7). The sample includes a healthy control group reported separately (I8). The paper computed within-task regulation contrasts (fear regulate > attend; OCD regulate > attend) (I9). Peak coordinates and group-level results are reported (tables and reference to supplemental whole-brain results), satisfying the whole-brain/map reporting requirement (I10,I11). Although the main analyses emphasize ROI/SVC results, the manuscript references supplemental whole-brain results and provides MNI coordinates in tables; therefore it provides the necessary whole-brain coordinates. Full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria from the meta-analysis (E4–E8) apply based on the provided content.

Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (use of cognitive reappraisal), I7 (static visual images: IAPS/photographs of people), I9 (reports within-task regulation contrasts, e.g., reappraise > look-negative), and I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with MNI coordinates reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I8 — the sample is a mixed adolescent/young-adult cohort (ages 15–25) and the paper does not report results for an adult-only healthy group separately; the review requires at least one group of healthy adults. Exclusion criteria met: none of E4–E8 apply. Full text appears complete and sufficient for screening.

This is a task-based fMRI study of healthy adults (N=60; resting-state N=48) that used cognitive reappraisal (explicit Increase and Decrease instructions) to regulate responses to static angry face photographs. The paper reports within-task whole-brain group contrasts related to reappraisal (e.g., Decrease > Observe-angry, Increase > Observe-angry) and provides peak coordinates in MNI space with cluster-level FWE correction. Stimuli are static images (FACES set). Healthy control participants are analyzed and reported separately. Resting-state analyses are also present but do not preclude inclusion because whole-brain task activation maps are reported. No exclusion criteria are met.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal in healthy adults (meets I5, I6, I8) and reports within-task contrasts (idea-generation RGT vs baseline and RGT>AUT; meets I9), it does NOT meet the stimulus criterion I7: the regulated stimuli are audio vignettes that participants were instructed to imagine (self-relevant anger-eliciting stories) with a brief matching photograph — regulation targeted imagined/autobiographical-like scenarios and auditory stories rather than regulation of static visual images alone. Therefore it fails the review’s required stimulus type. Additionally, the provided full text does not contain explicit peak coordinates/tables in the excerpt (Table 2 is referenced but coordinates are not shown), so I10 (explicit whole-brain peak coordinates reported in the provided text) cannot be verified from the provided content. Hence excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal using static IAPS images in a healthy adult sample, and it reports a within-task contrast (ReappNeg vs LookNeg). However, the paper's primary analyses are ROI-based (37 AAL ROIs) with PCA and discriminant analysis on ROI beta weights, and the full text does not provide a group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task activation map with peak coordinates in standard space. Therefore inclusion criterion I10 (whole-brain coordinates reported) is not met, and exclusion criterion E5 (only ROI analyses reported without a whole-brain map) applies. Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criteria not met: I10. Exclusion criteria applied: E5.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that explicitly implements cognitive reappraisal (down-regulation) of negative static visual images (IAPS). The paper reports within-task contrasts (Reappraise Negative > Attend/Look Negative) and whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses with peak coordinates in MNI space (tables and figures), meeting the meta-analysis requirements. The sample is healthy adults, methods and results are complete, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) with healthy adult participants (I8), using static visual images (I7), and it reports within-task contrasts and whole-brain peak coordinates for the appraisal contrast (like/dislike > male/female) (I9, I10, I11). However, the study’s regulation manipulation is appraisal/affect-labeling of one’s reaction (like/dislike) rather than an explicit reappraisal instruction (reinterpretation, perspective-taking with regulation goal, or distancing). The meta-analysis inclusion criterion I6 requires reappraisal (broadly construed to include reinterpretation, perspective-taking, distancing). Because the task does not implement explicit reappraisal (it probes appraisal/labeling without instructing participants to up- or down-regulate their emotional response), I6 is not met. Exclusion criteria: none of E4–E8 apply based on the full text. Therefore EXCLUDED.

This study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion requirements for the review. It used dynamic film clips (movies) rather than static visual images (violates I7), and the primary task-activation results are reported via ROI-extraction/analyses rather than a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map with peak coordinates (violates I10 / meets exclusion E5). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (reappraisal strategy used), I9 (within-task Regulate vs Attend contrasts were examined). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (stimuli are film clips, not static images), I8 (participants had prior psychiatric diagnoses reported in the sample, so the sample does not clearly meet the “no prior psychiatric disorder” stipulation), I10 (no whole-brain task activation peaks reported; analyses focused on ROI extractions). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (reporting only ROI analyses/without a whole-brain task activation map). Full text appears complete.

Based on the provided full text, the study meets several inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5); uses reappraisal/distancing as the regulation strategy (Decrease) (I6); uses static visual images (IAPS pictures) as stimuli (I7); includes healthy adult participants (I8); and reports within-task emotion-regulation contrasts (e.g., Decrease > Look-Negative; Decrease > Look-Neutral) (I9). However, the supplied article text does not provide peak coordinates for whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation maps in a standard stereotactic space (Talairach or MNI) despite noting that “coordinates refer to MNI” and reporting FWE thresholds; numeric peak coordinates/tables are absent from the provided content. Inclusion criterion I10 (reporting whole-brain peak coordinates) is therefore not satisfied on the basis of the provided material. No exclusion criteria from E4–E8 are met. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be satisfied, I must exclude this study from the meta-analysis on the basis of missing whole-brain peak coordinates in the provided full text (I10 not met).

This is a task-based fMRI study using an instructed causal-attribution emotion regulation paradigm (reinterpretation-like reappraisal) with static visual stimuli (faces). The authors report within-task regulation contrasts ([increase+decrease] > view) and whole-brain group-level analyses with peak activations (tables) and Monte-Carlo correction. However, the sample includes both patients with lifetime major depression and healthy controls, and the provided full text reports combined/group-level results across patients and controls rather than presenting whole-brain activation maps or peak coordinates reported separately for the healthy control group. The meta-analysis requires that, in studies including clinical samples, results for the healthy control group be reported separately (I8). Because healthy-control-only whole-brain coordinates/contrasts are not clearly reported in the available full text, the study does not meet inclusion criterion I8. No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) are triggered based on the provided content.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults who used cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate negative emotion elicited by static IAPS images. The paper reports within-task contrasts (regulate vs view) and a group-level whole-brain GLM for the localizer with peak coordinates reported (see Table 2, Talairach coordinates). Methods, participants (healthy adult sample), stimuli (static IAPS pictures), task (reappraisal/regulate blocks), and whole-brain results are all present in the full text. No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., it is empirical, not ROI-only, includes whole-brain maps and peak coordinates). Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Tables/Figures. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria listed below and should be included.

This is a task-based fMRI study using a reappraisal (distancing) strategy with static visual images (IAPS and photographs). The sample comprises healthy participants including adults (ages 6–23), participants aged 18+ are healthy adult subjects, and the paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., Reappraisal/Negative > Reactivity/Negative). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results with peak MNI coordinates are reported in tables and text (and supplementary material), fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, clinical-only reporting) apply.

This is a task-based pharmaco-fMRI study in healthy adults that used an explicit reappraisal instruction (Think Objectively) to down-regulate responses to static IAPS images and reports reappraise>watch contrasts and peak activations for ROI clusters. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (reappraisal strategy used), I7 (static visual images - IAPS), I8 (healthy adult sample), I9 (within-task reappraisal contrast reported), I11 (results reported in tables/figures). However, the authors conducted ROI-constrained analyses (a priori L amygdala and R IFG; a frontal AAL mask for exploratory analyses) and report ROI/region-limited peak results rather than a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map reported across the entire brain. Therefore the study does not meet I10 and falls under exclusion E5 (reports only ROI/masked analyses without an accompanying whole-brain map). Full text appears complete. Exclusion ID(s): E5. Inclusion IDs met: I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I11. Inclusion ID not met: I10.

This paper meets all inclusion criteria for the review: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that explicitly implements reappraisal (self-focused reappraisal) to both up- and down-regulate emotion (I6). The regulated stimuli are static visual images (angry and neutral faces from the FACES database) (I7). The sample includes a healthy adult control group reported separately (HC n=22) so healthy results can be extracted (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., increase > view-angry, decrease > view-angry) (I9). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are described with standard-space localization and cluster-level FWE thresholds; results are presented in tables/figures (implying reported peak coordinates in MNI/Talairach space) (I10,I11). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met. Thus the study should be INCLUDED.

The full text reports a task-based fMRI study that uses reappraisal (reduce emotion) to regulate responses to static negative images (IAPS). The sample includes a healthy control group reported separately. Group-level within-task contrasts (Reappraise and Maintain versus Baseline; HC > anxious) are voxelwise whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates provided in Talairach space (Tables 2 and 3). The methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text (fulltext complete). Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly implemented a reappraisal condition (reappraise > attend negative) using static visual images from the IAPS. The sample includes a healthy control group, and the paper defines and runs whole-brain, group-level contrasts (reappraise > attend negative) and reports main task effects and group differences (with results stated to be in Supplementary Materials), satisfying the requirement that whole-brain peak coordinates are reported (acceptable in supplementary materials per eligibility rules). The methods describe whole-brain voxelwise analyses and thresholds (FWE cluster-level correction), indicating standard group-level whole-brain reporting. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that includes an explicit Reappraisal condition and reports within-task, group-level whole-brain contrasts (e.g., Reappraisal > Watch-Negative) with whole-brain analysis details and referenced coordinate tables/supplementary material. Participants are healthy adult meditators. However, the emotional stimuli are dynamic film/video clips (10–12 s film clips), not static visual images as required by I7. Therefore the study fails inclusion criterion I7 and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that explicitly implemented cognitive reappraisal (distancing) during presentation of static visual images (IAPS). The sample comprised healthy younger and older adults with screening for neurological/psychiatric disorders. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., Reappraise > Experience and Experience > Reappraise) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates in MNI space (Tables and figures). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that explicitly implements reappraisal (down-regulation) as an emotion regulation strategy (reappraisal vs view contrasts). Stimuli are static visual images (IAPS photographs). The paper reports within-task group-level contrasts related to reappraisal (reappraisal emotional vs view emotional) and whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak activations reported in tables (MNI space, SPM5). All inclusion criteria are met (I5–I11). No exclusion criteria apply: whole-brain results are reported (not only ROI), task activation maps are provided (not only connectivity), and the sample consists of healthy adults with results reported for that group. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult women that implements a cognitive reappraisal-like strategy (LATER: consider long-term consequences) to down-regulate craving for palatable foods. Stimuli were static visual images (candy/dessert). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (LATER > NOW and OXT modulation) and provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results with peak MNI coordinates and FWE-corrected statistics. The full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria are met.

This full-text reports a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that implemented cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate negative affect (ERT using IAPS static images). The paper provides within-task contrasts for reappraisal (Reappraise > Look-Negative) at the group level and reports whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates in MNI space (multiple peak coordinates and volumes are listed; FWE-corrected results are reported). The sample is a healthy adult group (n=49) with clinical exclusions. The stimuli for the reappraisal task are static visual images. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5–I11) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is a task-based fMRI experiment in healthy adults using static IAPS images and reports whole-brain, group-level task contrasts with coordinates. However, the key emotion regulation strategy tested is mindfulness-based 'Observe' (objective observation and labeling) and expressive suppression, not reappraisal (reinterpretation, perspective-taking with an explicit goal to change emotional meaning). Thus it fails inclusion criterion I6 (reappraisal as the regulation strategy). 

(a) Exclusion IDs met: none ([])

(c) Inclusion IDs not met: I6 (reappraisal not implemented).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using a reappraisal-style distancing strategy to down-regulate responses to static IAPS images, and it reports within-task regulation contrasts (CER vs NoCER) and ROI/PPI results (meets I5, I6, I7, I8, I9). However, the full text as provided does not report a group-level whole-brain task-activation map for the reappraisal contrast with peak coordinates in standard space (I10 not satisfied). Instead, the paper focuses on seed-based PPI connectivity and ROI-extracted effects (ventral striatum ROI center reported) and relies on contrasts/seed definitions from a companion paper; no whole-brain peak coordinate tables for the regulation contrast are given. Therefore it falls under exclusion E6 (reports only seed-based/effective connectivity and ROI-focused results without an accompanying whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criteria not met: I10. Exclusion criteria met: E6.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study using cognitive reappraisal with static visual images and includes a healthy control group (I5, I6, I7, I8 satisfied), the paper does not report a group-level, whole-brain, within-task regulation contrast (e.g., Reappraise > Look) with peak coordinates for the healthy control sample alone. The reported whole-brain coordinates are for a Group × Condition interaction and between-group comparisons, rather than a standalone healthy-group reappraisal activation map. Therefore inclusion criteria I9 and I10 are not met. This study effectively reports only between-group/interactions for the reported peaks, fitting exclusion criterion E7.

Full text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (reappraisal used as regulation), I8 (healthy adult control group included), I9 (within-task reappraisal contrast reported: REAPPRAISAL > NO REAPPRAISAL). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I7 (stimuli are 1.5s video clips of laughing faces, not static visual images), I10 (the key reported reappraisal effect was an ROI-based result in left DLPFC; whole-brain analysis yielded no significant task-activation peaks for the reappraisal contrast, so a qualifying group-level whole-brain task activation map with reported peak coordinates is not provided for the main activation finding). No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) from the review list were directly triggered. Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails to meet mandatory inclusion criteria I7 and I10.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly used cognitive reappraisal (Regulate vs Maintain) to down-regulate negative emotion (I5, I6). The regulated stimuli were static visual images from the IAPS (I7). Participants were healthy young adults (normal-weight and excess-weight groups) with psychiatric/medical exclusions, so at least one healthy adult group is available (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (Regulate/Maintain) (I9). Group-level SPM analyses and peak coordinates are reported (including MNI coordinates for insula seeds and between-group activation peaks), and whole-brain/PPI analyses were conducted (I10, I11). Full text sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) are present and complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) apply based on provided information. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is eligible for the review.

E4-E8: none met. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (reappraisal implemented), I8 (healthy adult sample), I9 (within-task regulation contrasts reported), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps with peak coordinates), I11 (coordinates reported in tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 — stimuli are 15-sec film/video clips, not static visual images as required by the review objective, so the study does not qualify.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation that directly compares reappraisal and acceptance using static sad images (IAPS and other pictures) and includes a healthy control group reported separately. It reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., reappraise > view) and whole-brain mixed-effects analyses. Thus I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9 are satisfied. However, the provided full text does not include peak coordinates in a standard stereotaxic space (Talairach or MNI) in the excerpt (tables are referenced but numeric coordinates are not present here), so I cannot verify I10 (reported whole-brain peak coordinates). Because I10 is a required inclusion criterion and cannot be confirmed from the provided content, the study must be excluded. Full text appears otherwise complete (methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is a task-based fMRI experiment that directly compares cognitive reappraisal and placebo regulation. Reappraisal was explicitly implemented as a down-regulation strategy and practiced by participants. The regulated stimuli were static visual images (IAPS pictures). Participants were healthy adults, and results for the healthy groups are reported separately. The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., RU–CUR, CUR–RU) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates reported in standard space (MNI/Talairach) in tables/figures. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study using reappraisal of static IAPS pictures and includes a healthy low-risk group, the paper does not report a within-group, whole-brain reappraisal contrast (e.g., reappraise>maintain) with peak coordinates specifically for the healthy control/low-risk sample. The manuscript reports main effects across all participants and between-group comparisons (high-risk vs low-risk), but does not provide a standalone group-level task activation map/peak coordinates for the healthy control group that could be entered into the meta-analysis. Therefore inclusion criterion I9 (within-task contrast reported for the target healthy sample) is not met, so the study cannot be included. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I10. Inclusion criterion not met: I9. No exclusion criteria from the list are directly violated.

Full text reports a task-based fMRI experiment using cognitive reappraisal (down-regulation) of negative IAPS images (static visual stimuli). The paper includes a separate group of combat-exposed controls (no PTSD) reported independently, satisfying the requirement for a healthy adult sample. The analysis contains within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (Reappraise > Maintain) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates in MNI space (tables/figures), in addition to ROI analyses. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria relevant to the review are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that explicitly instructs participants to use cognitive reappraisal (decrease) to regulate emotion (I6) while viewing static visual images from the IAPS (I7). The sample is healthy adults with exclusions for pathology and results reported for the healthy group (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (decrease-negative > look-negative) (I9) and conducts whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with reported peak coordinates/cluster locations in standard (MNI) space (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) apply: the study is empirical, includes whole-brain maps rather than ROI-only or connectivity-only results, and reports within-subject regulation contrasts rather than only between-group contrasts. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore I include this study for the meta-analysis.

This study does not use reappraisal (or reinterpretation/distancing with an explicit regulation goal). It employs an approach–avoidance task probing emotional action control, not instructions to reappraise/ up- or down-regulate emotional responses; thus I6 is not met. It also does not report any within-task reappraisal contrast such as “reappraise > look” (I9 not met). It does meet several other inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI (I5), static visual stimuli (faces) (I7), healthy adult sample reported separately (police recruits) (I8), and reports whole-brain MNI peak coordinates for task effects (I10). No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) apply. Therefore the study is ineligible for this meta-analysis because it lacks the required reappraisal manipulation and corresponding regulation contrasts.

Excluded because the regulated stimuli are dynamic video clips rather than static visual images (violates I7), and the sample consists of daily young-adult smokers meeting criteria for nicotine dependence rather than a healthy non-clinical adult sample (violates I8). The study does satisfy several inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (uses distancing, a reappraisal-style strategy), I9 (reports within-task regulation contrasts, e.g., close vs. far), I10 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster results and peak coordinates reported in Table S1), and I11 (coordinates/results reported in supplementary materials). No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation that uses reappraisal of static IAPS pictures (decrease vs look) and reports voxel-wise analyses, but the primary sample consists of individuals with PTSD, not healthy adults. Although a separate healthy sample (N=14) was scanned with concurrent TMS-fMRI, those healthy participants did not perform the reappraisal task; thus no healthy adult task-based reappraisal activation results are reported. (a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (reappraisal strategy), I7 (static visual images), I9 (within-task regulation contrast reported), I10 (voxelwise whole-brain analyses reported), I11 (results/tables/supplement reporting noted). (c) Inclusion IDs NOT met: I8 (no healthy adult group with task reappraisal results reported separately). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore EXCLUDED because it fails I8.

This is a task-based fMRI study of healthy adults using static face images (Face Matching Task) and reports group-level whole-brain GLM results (coordinates in Supplementary Table S2). Therefore it meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (static visual stimuli), I8 (healthy adult sample), and reports whole-brain maps/coordinates (I10, I11). However, the study does NOT implement any emotion regulation (reappraisal) manipulation or instructions (the task is implicit face identity matching), so it fails I6 (reappraisal as regulation strategy). It also does not report any within-task emotion-regulation contrast (e.g., reappraise > look), so it fails I9. No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) apply. Because key inclusion criteria I6 and I9 are not met, the study must be excluded.

Although this is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that implements instructed reappraisal and reports within-task contrasts and whole-brain results, the emotional stimuli being regulated are social/monetary decision outcomes in the Ultimatum Game (i.e., offers and proposers' behavior), not static visual images. Inclusion criterion I7 explicitly excludes studies regulating monetary or social decision outcomes. Thus the study fails I7 and must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

This is an event-related task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants that explicitly implemented cognitive reappraisal ("decrease" instruction; reinterpretation/situation-focused reappraisal) to down-regulate emotion in response to static visual images (IAPS and matched photographs). It reports within-task contrasts (e.g., reappraise > look negative, reappraise > distract) and group-level whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates (e.g., amygdala and prefrontal peaks reported in MNI/Talairach-style coordinates and coordinate tables/figures). Participants were healthy adults (screened for psychiatric diagnoses). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The provided full text is limited to an abstract-level summary and does not include methods/results tables with peak coordinates. From the abstract, the study appears to be a task-based fMRI reappraisal study using static pictures in healthy adults and reports regulation contrasts, so I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 appear satisfied. However, I cannot verify that group-level whole-brain voxelwise peak coordinates are reported (I10). Because the full text is incomplete, I cannot confirm whole-brain coordinate reporting, so the study is excluded pending full-text verification.

This is a task-based fMRI study that implemented cognitive reappraisal (reappraising vs attending-negative) using static visual images from the IAPS. The sample includes a healthy control group reported separately and within-group and between-group contrasts are provided (e.g., reappraising > attending-negative). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted and peak activations are reported in tables (Tables S1–S4 referenced), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain coordinates in standard space. The paper also reports GLM activation results and DCM effective connectivity, but the presence of whole-brain activation maps and coordinates means it is not excluded by connectivity-only criteria. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present in the provided text.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using instructed cognitive reappraisal (I6) to down-regulate emotion; stimuli are static photographs of faces (NimStim) (I7); the sample is screened healthy adults with results reported for the control group (I8); the paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (Reappraise-Neg vs Maintain-Neg and others) (I9); analyses used whole-brain, group-level voxelwise maps normalized to MNI space with peak coordinates reported (Table 1 referenced) (I10), and results/coordinates are clearly described in text/tables (I11). This is a task fMRI study using cognitive reappraisal with a healthy control group, but it does not meet the review’s core requirements: stimuli are dynamic video clips (not static images) violating I7, and the paper reports ROI-based network/connectivity analyses (DEPNA) rather than whole-brain, voxelwise task activation maps with peak coordinates, violating I10 and matching exclusion criteria for ROI/connectivity-only results (E5, E6). This study meets all inclusion requirements for the meta-analysis. This is a task-based fMRI study using a reappraisal emotion-regulation paradigm (reappraise vs maintain) with static visual IAPS images. This full-text reports a 2-day task-based fMRI experiment in healthy adult participants using cognitive reappraisal (up- and down-regulation) to regulate emotions elicited by static visual images (IAPS and internet pictures). Although this is a task-based fMRI study using self-focused reappraisal (distancing and increasing) with static visual IAPS images and reports whole-brain, peak-coordinate results, it involves a clinical sample (SAD) alongside healthy controls but does not report the healthy control group’s task activation maps/contrast coordinates separately in the main text. This full text reports a task-based fMRI experiment (Experiment 3) in which healthy adult participants used cognitive reappraisal (increase, maintain, decrease) to regulate emotion elicited by static visual images (IAPS). This study does not meet the key reappraisal criterion (I6). This is a task-based fMRI study using cognitive reappraisal (explicit 'decrease' instructions) to down-regulate negative emotion elicited by static visual images (IAPS and child picture set). This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=58) using instruction-induced reappraisal (reinterpretation) to down-regulate emotion in response to static visual images (IAPS). Thus it meets the review’s requirements for task, strategy, stimulus type, healthy sample, regulation contrasts, and whole-brain coordinate reporting.

This is a task-based fMRI study using cognitive reappraisal (Increase/Decrease) to regulate emotions elicited by static visual images (IAPS). Sample comprises healthy adults (n=23) with no neurological/psychiatric history. The paper reports within-task contrasts (Increase > Look-Negative; Decrease > Look-Negative) from a whole-brain GLM transformed into Talairach space and provides peak coordinates for ROIs (e.g., left IFG: −45,26,7) and whole-brain thresholding/cluster results (figures/tables referenced). This is a task-based fMRI study of emotion regulation using static IAPS images and a reappraisal-like instruction (‘‘diminish’’ = imagine a less-negative outcome). It includes a healthy control group. However, the paper’s reported results and the provided full text focus on between-group comparisons (PTSD vs. controls) rather than reporting within-sample (healthy-controls) whole-brain regulation contrasts (e.g., reappraise>maintain) or presenting peak coordinates for such whole-brain maps. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E7 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8. Inclusion criteria not met: I9 (no clear within-task/regulation contrast reported for the healthy control group in the provided text) and I10 (no peak coordinates for whole-brain group-level maps for the healthy sample are present in the provided full text).

This is a task fMRI study in healthy adults that uses a cognitive reappraisal-like strategy (‘reality checking’) and reports whole-brain, group-level coordinates. However it does NOT meet key inclusion criteria: the instructed regulation was applied during the anticipation period (cues) rather than to the static visual images themselves—i.e. the regulated stimuli are anticipatory cues/anticipatory state rather than the static pictures (violates I7). Further, the manipulation is implemented as a between-subjects strategy comparison (cognitive-control group vs basic group) rather than a within-task regulation contrast such as reappraise > look or down-regulate > maintain within the same participants, so there is no explicit within-task regulation contrast isolating reappraisal (violates I9). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (reappraisal-like strategy used), I8 (healthy adult sample), I10 (group-level whole-brain maps with coordinates), I11 (results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria from E4–E8 are directly met.

This is a task-based fMRI study of healthy adults (n=30) using a standard cognitive reappraisal paradigm to down-regulate negative emotion elicited by static visual IAPS images. Participants were healthy and results for the healthy sample are presented. No exclusion criteria are met (the study includes whole-brain maps and is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not a review, and not a between-group-only report). Full text appears complete.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that explicitly uses cognitive reappraisal instructions to downregulate negative affect (I6) while participants view static IAPS images (I7). A healthy control group is reported separately alongside a clinical group, enabling extraction of healthy adult results (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (Reappraise vs Maintain; I9). Analyses include group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistics with multiple-comparison correction, and MNI peak coordinates are reported for key seeds/ROIs and connectivity clusters, consistent with I10; whole-brain task effects are described and results are presented in text/tables/figures (I11). No exclusion criteria are met (none of E4–E8 apply). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly implemented an emotion regulation task including a reappraise instruction (Sad-Reappraise vs Sad-View). Participants were adult females screened with SCID and without MDD (non-clinical/subclinical sample), satisfying the healthy adult sample requirement. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I5–I11. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (not incomplete). No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that explicitly implements a cognitive reappraisal instruction (REAP: “pretend unreal”) to down-regulate emotion (I6). This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that implemented an incidental/implicit cognitive reappraisal manipulation (non-negative vs negative preceding descriptions) to down-regulate emotional responses to static visual images (IAPS). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing assessment of eligibility.

This study meets multiple inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5), implements reappraisal as an explicit regulation condition (REAP) (I6), uses static visual images (I7), tests healthy adult participants (I8), and reports whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates (I10) (coordinates for multiple clusters are provided in the text) and figures/tables (I11). However, the paper does not report a clear within-task emotion-regulation contrast of the form required by the review (e.g., reappraise > look, down-regulate > maintain) at the group whole-brain level in this manuscript. The authors state that main effects of regulation strategies are described in a separate report, and the present article reports parametric/modulation analyses (social vs nonsocial within each viewing condition) and correlations with attachment measures rather than an explicit REAP > NAT (or equivalent) contrast suitable for inclusion per I9. Therefore I exclude this article because it does not meet inclusion criterion I9 (within-task regulation contrast reported here).

All inclusion criteria are satisfied: the study is a task-based fMRI experiment (I5) that explicitly uses cognitive reappraisal/reinterpretation to down-regulate negative emotion (I6). Although this is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports within-task regulation contrasts and whole-brain coordinates (see Methods, Results, and Table 2), the emotion regulation manipulation is an imagery-focused strategy (instructing participants to imagine a calming or exciting scene) rather than reappraisal (e.g., reinterpretation, perspective-taking, or distancing). No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) apply. Therefore the study is excluded because it does not implement reappraisal as defined by the review (I6 not met).

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that implements cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate craving (I6); regulated stimuli are static visual food images (I7); participants are healthy adults with exclusions for neurological/psychiatric disorders and results are reported for this group (I8); the paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., Regulate > Look, RC > LC) (I9); analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise, and peak coordinates are reported in MNI space (I10); whole-brain results and coordinates are clearly described in text/tables (I11). Although this is a task-based fMRI study of healthy adults using reappraisal to down-regulate emotions elicited by static visual images (I5, I6, I7, I8) and it reports within-task contrasts for regulation (reappraisal vs. watching) used in ROI analyses (I9), the paper does not report a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) statistical map with peak coordinates for the reappraisal/regulation contrasts. This paper is a task-based fMRI study using an established reappraisal paradigm (increase/decrease instructions) with static visual images from the IAPS. This study is a task-based fMRI investigation (I5) that explicitly used cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate emotion (I6) while participants viewed static sad images drawn from IAPS and other normed picture sets (I7). This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=17 analyzed) that implemented cognitive reappraisal (distancing) to downregulate emotion to static visual images (IAPS photographs). This study should be excluded because it does not implement reappraisal of static visual images. This is a task-based fMRI study of healthy adults viewing static negative faces (I5, I7, I8 met). However, the task did not instruct participants to perform cognitive reappraisal; the authors infer spontaneous/implicit reappraisal by correlating participants’ face>shape whole-brain maps with an independently derived reappraisal meta-analytic map. Although this is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using static visual images, reporting within-task contrasts and whole-brain coordinates, the emotion-regulation strategy investigated is emotional suppression (instructions to inhibit experience/expression and priming for suppression). The review requires reappraisal (reinterpretation, perspective-taking, distancing) as the regulation strategy (I6). This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using static facial images (I5, I7, I8 satisfied). However, the study did not implement an in-scanner reappraisal emotion-regulation manipulation or provide any within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., “reappraise > look”) — it used passive viewing and assessed reappraisal only via a self-report questionnaire (violates I6 and I9). Analytically, the authors focused on a region-of-interest (ROI) approach (with ROI-controlled inference) rather than reporting a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map; although peak coordinates are reported for ROI clusters, no accompanying whole-brain voxelwise map/analysis is provided (violates I10). Because the paper reports only ROI-based task activation results without an accompanying whole-brain map, it meets exclusion criterion E5. Therefore the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria for the review and must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that used a reappraisal strategy (distancing) delivered socially (psychotherapist) to down-regulate emotion elicited by static visual images (IAPS). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet I6 (reappraisal as the regulation strategy).

This study is excluded because it does not meet key intervention/stimulus criteria for the review. Although it is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study that reports within-task regulation contrasts in a healthy elderly control group, the emotion-regulation manipulation is NOT reappraisal: it uses worry induction/suppression via personalized textual worry scripts and prompted imagery of pleasant memories (suppression/distraction), not reinterpretation/distancing/reappraisal of an emotional stimulus. Also, the regulated stimuli are personalized written sentences and imagined memories rather than static visual images (e.g., IAPS pictures or photographs). Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I7. Exclusion criteria met: none ([]).

This study does not use reappraisal (reinterpretation, perspective-taking, or distancing) as the instructed emotion-regulation strategy. Although the study is task-based fMRI (I5), uses static visual images (I7), includes a healthy adult sample reported separately (I8), reports within-task contrasts (maintain vs non-maintain) and provides whole-brain group results with peak coordinates (I10, I11), it does not implement or report reappraisal-based regulation contrasts (I6) and thus does not meet the review’s core intervention criterion. No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) are triggered by the full text. Therefore the paper must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using static visual images (I7) and includes a healthy control group reported separately (I8). It reports whole-brain, group-level task activation maps with peak coordinates (I10) and presents coordinate tables/figures (I11). This is a task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal in healthy adults that reports whole-brain, voxelwise activation contrasts and coordinate tables; however the regulation targets internally-recalled images (participants recalled previously encoded IAPS pictures from memory while regulating), not externally presented static visual stimuli during scanning. This full text meets all inclusion criteria for the review: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using instructed cognitive reappraisal (down- and up-regulation) as the regulation strategy (I6); stimuli were static visual images from the IAPS (I7); participants were healthy adult volunteers with exclusion of psychiatric/medical disorders and results reported for these healthy groups (I8); the paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (downregulate vs look, upregulate vs look) (I9); analyses include whole-brain, voxelwise RFX ANOVA group-level maps with peak coordinates reported in Talairach space (I10), and results/tables describing whole-brain findings are included (I11).
