This full text meets all review inclusion criteria: it reports a task-based fMRI experiment using cognitive reappraisal (distancing) to down-regulate negative emotion (I5,I6). Stimuli were static visual images (Emotional Picture Set) (I7). Sample comprises healthy adults (n=108) with exclusions and demographics described (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts of interest (e.g., RegulateNeg > WatchNeg; WatchNeg > RegulateNeg) (I9). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (RegulateNeg > WatchNeg whole-brain FWE-corrected) and peak coordinates/MNI locations are provided in-text and in supplementary tables (e.g., amygdala and parietal peaks), satisfying the requirement for standard-space coordinates (I10,I11). Full text includes methods, results, and discussion; supplementary tables are referenced for coordinate lists. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study is excluded because it does not implement a reappraisal emotion-regulation task and does not use static visual images as regulated stimuli. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (healthy adult control group reported separately), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with Talairach coordinates reported). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no reappraisal/reinterpretation/perspective-taking/distancing instruction — participants only judged valence), I7 (stimuli are auditory: musical and nonmusical sounds, not static visual images), I9 (no within-task contrast indexing reappraisal vs. baseline/maintain because no regulation instruction was used). No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) are directly triggered by the manuscript. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The full text meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that explicitly uses cognitive reappraisal as the emotion regulation strategy (I6) with static visual images from the IAPS (I7). The sample comprises healthy adults screened for psychiatric/medical disorders (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (Reappraise vs Maintain) and uses these contrasts in second-level analyses (I9). Group-level, voxelwise analyses are reported and peak coordinates are provided in standard MNI space (I10), and coordinates/figures/tables are described in the text (I11). Although ROI/SVC analyses were used for some hypotheses, the authors also report whole-brain voxelwise results and provide MNI coordinates for peak activations and connectivity clusters, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain coordinate reporting. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study that implemented cognitive reappraisal (distancing) to down-regulate negative emotion using static visual images (IAPS and similar photographs). The sample consists of healthy participants including adults (ages up to 22.9) and results are reported as within-task contrasts (e.g., regulation/negative > reactivity/negative). The paper reports whole-brain group-level analyses and peak coordinates (amygdala coordinates and other clusters; supplementary tables and tables described), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps in standard space. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing assessment of criteria.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5); uses reappraisal as the emotion-regulation strategy (instructing participants to ignore facial expression and rate attractiveness — I6); regulated stimuli are static visual images (KDEF photos of faces — I7); sample consists of healthy adults (n=18) with no reported disorders (I8); reports within-task contrast comparing high-control (reappraise) > low-control (rate) for the emotion domain (I9); and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates in MNI space (I10). No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Full text contains methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This paper meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using cognitive reappraisal (including distancing/perspective-taking) to up- and down-regulate negative emotion (I6). Stimuli were static visual images from the IAPS (I7). The sample comprises healthy adult participants with results reported for the healthy group (I8). The manuscript reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., increase > look, decrease > look) (I9) and provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps with peak coordinates in standard (MNI/ICBM) space and tables of coordinates (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) are met. Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that implemented reappraisal via the distancing strategy while participants viewed static IAPS images of social (interpersonal) scenes. The design crossed instruction (distance vs. look) with stimulus valence (negative vs. neutral) and reports within-task contrasts (e.g., distance > look, look > distance) for the healthy control group. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (SPM2) with cluster-correction and results reported with peak coordinates in MNI space (tables/figures). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or empathy-without-regulation) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review objective.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants using a detachment (distancing/perspective-taking) strategy to intentionally downregulate emotion in response to static IAPS pictures. The paper reports within-task regulation versus permit (no-regulation) contrasts, group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (with FWE correction) and peak coordinates for amygdala and other activations (standard space). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults directly testing reappraisal strategies (Reinterpretation and Detachment) using static visual images (IAPS). The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., ‘Regulate Negative’ > ‘Permit Negative’ and reverse) at the group level with whole-brain voxelwise analyses and peak coordinates (MNI), and presents results in main text/tables. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I5–I11 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study using a cognitive reappraisal paradigm (Suppress vs Maintain) with static IAPS images. The sample includes a healthy control group (non-drug-using controls) and the paper reports the relevant within-task contrasts (Maintain>Observe and Suppress>Maintain). The authors performed group-level whole-brain voxel-wise analyses (in addition to ROI/SVC tests) with cluster-level correction and indicate that detailed one-sample task activations and between-group whole-brain comparisons (with coordinates) are provided in Supplementary Tables S1–S7. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I5–I10 (and I11). No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) apply.

This article reports a task-based fMRI study in which participants were trained to use cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate emotion (Reduce vs Maintain), using static IAPS images as stimuli. The sample includes a healthy control group (Normal Anxiety; no history of mood/anxiety disorders). Whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted (AlphaSim correction) and significant clusters from the Reduce>Maintain contrast and group contrasts are reported in tables/figures, indicating peak coordinates in standard space. Thus the study meets the meta-analysis requirements for task-based reappraisal with static visual stimuli in healthy adults and provides whole-brain coordinate results.

This is a task-based fMRI study that used reappraisal strategies (increase by engaging; decrease by distancing) to regulate emotion elicited by static visual images (IAPS threat-related pictures). The sample comprised healthy adult participants (n=24, females) with results reported for the healthy group. The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (increase > view, decrease > view, view > decrease) and presents group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with peak coordinates in MNI space (tables and figures). Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

Full text reviewed and is complete. This study is excluded because the emotion-regulation strategy examined is distraction (memorize vs. view), not reappraisal (reinterpretation, distancing, or perspective-taking). While the paper is a task-based fMRI study using static visual images, includes a healthy control group, and reports whole-brain peak coordinates, it does not implement or report a reappraisal-based regulation contrast (e.g., reappraise > look) for the healthy adults. Therefore it fails the critical inclusion criteria I6 (reappraisal strategy) and I9 (within-task reappraisal contrast). No exclusion criteria from E4–E8 apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that explicitly implemented cognitive reappraisal (positive reappraisal) to downregulate emotional responses to static IAPS images. The manuscript reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., [view NEG – reappraise]) and random-effects group analyses. Although primary ROI/SVC analyses are emphasized, the paper states complementary exploratory whole-brain analyses are provided in the supplementary material (Supplementary Table 1) and reports peak voxel locations for contrasts, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, group-level task activation maps with coordinates. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext complete). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, patient-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is eligible for the meta-analysis.

Meets all inclusion criteria: (I5) This is a task-based fMRI study; (I6) Explicit reappraisal instructions (MAINTAIN/INCREASE/DECREASE) implemented as reinterpretation/distancing strategies; (I7) Emotional stimuli are static visual images (IAPS photographs and similar pictures); (I8) Includes a healthy adult control group (n=15) with results reported separately and compared to patients; (I9) Reports within-task regulation contrasts (DECREASE > MAINTAIN; INCREASE > MAINTAIN) and related analyses; (I10) Presents group-level, whole-brain task activation results with peak coordinates reported in MNI space (tables and text; Supplement noted for within-group contrasts); (I11) Whole-brain results and coordinates are provided in the main text/tables and referenced supplementary material. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; core content appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) apply. Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis focusing on reappraisal of static visual stimuli in healthy adults.

The study reports a task-based fMRI investigation using cognitive reappraisal of static visual food images with whole-brain group-level contrasts and coordinates (meets I5, I6, I7, I9, I10, I11). However, the sample is a developmental cohort of females aged 10–23 and the analyses are reported across the full mixed-age sample; no separate group-level results restricted to a healthy adult-only group are reported. The meta-analysis requires at least one group of healthy adults with results reported separately (I8), which is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

Although this is an empirical, task-based simultaneous EEG-fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal in healthy adults using static visual IAPS images (meeting I5–I8) and it reports within-task comparisons related to reappraisal (I9), the fMRI results are reported at the AAL ROI level (mean ROI Z-scores) and via KCCA/GLM summaries rather than as group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps with peak coordinates in a standard space. No MNI/Talairach peak coordinates or whole-brain voxelwise maps are provided. Therefore it fails I10 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only reporting). Full text appears complete.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study of reappraisal in healthy adults using static visual images and reports within-task contrasts, it does not report group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps with peak coordinates. Analyses rely on ROI-based amygdala activation and PPI connectivity restricted to IFG masks; whole-brain task-evoked coordinates for the reappraisal contrast are not provided. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E5 (ROI/restricted analyses without accompanying whole-brain map). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (reappraisal used), I7 (static visual image stimuli), I8 (healthy adult control group reported), I9 (within-task regulation contrast reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I10 (group-level whole-brain task activation map with peak coordinates). Full text appears complete.

The full text describes a task-based fMRI experiment in healthy adult participants (26 women) that instructs participants to use cognitive reappraisal to decrease negative affect (reappraise vs look). The regulation was applied while viewing static visual face stimuli (neutral faces presented during the instruction period), fulfilling the stimulus requirement. The paper reports within-task contrasts relating to regulation (e.g., reappraise > look) and performs whole-brain, voxelwise analyses with cluster thresholds and reports coordinates/tables and figures. The sample excludes psychiatric/neurological disorders and presents group-level whole-brain results for the healthy group. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the provided content is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study does not investigate reappraisal-based emotion regulation. Participants performed an attentional spatial-cueing task and were instructed to ignore emotional face distracters rather than to reappraise, so I6 (reappraisal used) is not met. The paper does not report any within-task reappraisal vs control contrasts (e.g., reappraise > look), so I9 (within-task regulation contrast) is not met. Analyses focus on ACC and PFC using anatomical masks and small-volume correction rather than reporting a group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation map, so it fails I10 and meets exclusion E5 (ROI/SVC-only results without whole-brain map). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (regulated stimuli are static visual images—faces), I8 (healthy adult sample), and I11 (peak coordinates are reported for reported activations). Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I9, I10. Exclusion criteria met: E5. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion are present). Thus the study should be excluded from the meta-analysis.

The study meets several inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI experiment (I5) that explicitly implemented reappraisal as an emotion regulation strategy (I6) while participants viewed static visual images from the IAPS (I7). The sample includes a healthy control group reported separately and within-group analyses (I8), and the paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (reappraise vs. view; I9). However, the fMRI analyses were conducted using anatomically defined ROIs (AAL masks) and activations were examined/thresholded within these ROIs (methods state that ROIs were used for all analyses). There is no clear indication of a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map reported (I10 not met). Because results appear to be ROI-restricted (or small-volume corrected) without accompanying whole-brain maps, this triggers exclusion criterion E5. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Thus the study is excluded for failing I10 and meeting E5.

This study must be excluded because the regulated stimuli are personalized worry sentences (textual/narrative scripts) presented on-screen, not static visual images such as IAPS photographs (fails I7). Although the study is task-based neuroimaging (I5), implements reappraisal as an emotion-regulation strategy (I6), includes a healthy older adult control group reported separately (I8), and reports within-task reappraisal contrasts (reappraisal vs rest) (I9), the stimulus modality requirement is not met. Additionally, the provided full text does not contain explicit whole-brain peak coordinates in standard space so I10 cannot be verified from the supplied content. Therefore it does not satisfy all inclusion criteria.

Full text is complete. Met inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (static visual images used), I8 (healthy adult sample reported separately), I9 (within-task regulation contrasts reported, e.g., PosUp > PosWatch), I10 (group-level whole-brain analyses with coordinates in MNI space reported), I11 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables). Did NOT meet I6: the task instructed participants to ‘up-regulate’ affect but explicitly stated that no specific emotion regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, reinterpretation, perspective-taking, distancing) was instructed; therefore the study does not implement reappraisal (broadly construed) as the controlled strategy required by the review. No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) apply. Conclusion: EXCLUDE due to failure to meet I6 (reappraisal requirement).

Full text is incomplete/unavailable (API error in provided full text), preventing verification of methods and results. Based on title/metadata this appears to be an fMRI study of lorazepam effects in catatonia rather than a reappraisal task in healthy adults. Exclusion IDs met: none (E4- E8 not confirmed). Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met / could not be confirmed: I5 (task details not confirmed), I6 (no evidence reappraisal was used), I7 (stimulus type not confirmed as static visual images), I8 (target sample likely clinical rather than healthy adults or healthy controls not reported separately), I9 (within-task regulation contrast not confirmed), I10 (whole-brain coordinates not reported/confirmed). fulltext_incomplete=true; cannot include without complete article confirming criteria.

This fMRI study is task-based (I5), uses static visual images as stimuli (I7), includes a healthy control group reported separately (I8), and reports within-task contrasts comparing strategies (evaluation vs distraction), i.e., a regulation contrast (distraction > evaluation / evaluation > distraction) (I9). However, the emotion regulation strategy tested is attentional distraction (bar-orientation task), not reappraisal (reinterpretation, perspective-taking, or distancing), so it fails inclusion criterion I6. In addition, the provided full text does not report whole-brain peak coordinates in a standard space (Talairach/MNI) for the regulation contrasts (I10 not met). No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) appear to apply. Therefore the study must be excluded because it does not implement reappraisal (I6) and does not clearly provide whole-brain peak coordinates (I10).

Meets all inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI with an emotion regulation manipulation using reappraisal/distancing (detachment) among strategies; stimuli are static IAPS images; sample includes healthy adult participants (n=55, females) with results reported for this group; within-task contrasts of regulation versus look/unregulated (e.g., Stim_RegAv>Stim_Av) are reported; group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FWE correction and peak coordinates in standard MNI space are provided. Full text contains methods, results, and reported peak coordinates, enabling extraction for meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that implemented cognitive reappraisal as an explicit emotion-regulation strategy (I6). The regulated stimuli were static visual images (IAPS pictures) (I7). The sample comprised healthy adult participants (42 screened females) with psychiatric/medical exclusions (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts involving reappraisal (e.g., Target Reappraisal > Target Appraise) (I9) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates in MNI space reported in tables (FWE-corrected) (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria are met: this is empirical original data (not E4), includes whole-brain analyses (not E5), is not limited to connectivity or resting-state (not E6), and reports within-task contrasts rather than only between-group effects (not E7); the reappraisal instruction includes an explicit regulation goal (not E8). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria listed and none of the exclusion criteria.

This full text reports a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using reappraisal of static visual images (IAPS) with a block-design emotion regulation task. The sample includes healthy adults (n=49 analyzed). The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing Reappraise versus Maintain and presents whole-brain group-level activation and connectivity analyses, with activation results and coordinate tables/figures (Tables 2 and 3 and Supplement) at voxelwise thresholds. Thus it meets the review’s requirements for reappraisal of static visual stimuli, healthy adult sample, within-task contrasts, and whole-brain peak coordinates. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, supplementary data).

This study is excluded because the target sample does not meet the review’s population criterion: participants are adolescents (mean age 15.2), not healthy adults (I8 not met). The article otherwise meets several inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (cognitive reappraisal strategies used), I7 (static visual image stimuli), and I9 (within-task regulation contrasts reported). I10 (reporting of whole-brain peak coordinates) appears not to be satisfied in the provided full text — the results describe activated regions but no peak coordinates are given; if coordinates are present elsewhere in supplemental materials not provided here this could change eligibility. No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) were triggered by the available text. Full text appears complete for core sections. Thus excluded primarily for I8 (age group) and possibly I10 (coordinates absent).

This study meets multiple inclusion criteria relevant to the review: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5); uses cognitive reappraisal as the regulation strategy (I6); the stimuli are static visual images (I7); reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., reappraise > look-negative; I9); provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported peak coordinates in standard (MNI) space (I10) and presents whole-brain results described in text/tables (I11). However, it does NOT meet I8: the target sample requirement of healthy adults. Although a healthy control group is reported separately, controls are a youth sample with ages 15–25 (including minors <18), so the study does not provide an exclusively healthy-adult sample required by the meta-analysis objective. No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) are triggered by the manuscript. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be excluded for failing to meet I8.

All inclusion criteria are met: (I5) This is an empirical task-based fMRI study; (I6) the task explicitly uses reappraisal (positive reappraisal and minimizing reappraisal) as emotion regulation tactics; (I7) the regulated stimuli are static visual images drawn from the IAPS; (I8) the sample comprises healthy adult participants (screened for psychiatric disorder) and a separate healthy behavioral cohort; (I9) the paper reports within-task regulation contrasts and parametric effects (e.g., positive reappraisal > natural response, minimizing reappraisal > natural response); (I10) group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with peak coordinates in standard space and whole-brain corrected maps; (I11) results are clearly described in text and figures/tables. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study that implemented cognitive reappraisal (Regulate/Decrease cue) to down-regulate emotion in response to static visual images (negative and neutral scenes). The sample comprised healthy adults with no DSM-IV Axis-I psychiatric or cardiovascular/immune disorders. The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (Regulate Negative > Look Negative) and presents whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (with whole-brain effects and coordinate tables reported in the supplement). All inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met, and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

The full text reports a task-based fMRI experiment in healthy adults (final N=20) using self-focused reappraisal (distancing) to down-regulate negative emotion elicited by static IAPS pictures. The task includes the appropriate within-task contrast for regulation (Decrease > LookNeg). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported with peak coordinates (MNI) and tables/figures, and ROI results are additionally presented. Participants were healthy volunteers with exclusion of neurological/psychiatric history. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion, tables/supplement referenced).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=51) that implements an explicit reappraisal condition (Reappraise vs Attend Negative). Stimuli are static visual images from the IAPS. The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (Reappraise > Attend/Attend Negative) and performs whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses with peak coordinates reported in tables and supplementary materials (with cluster-level FWE correction and coordinates in MNI space; an amygdala SVC was applied for some tests but whole-brain results are also reported). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; core data needed for screening are present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly implements instructed cognitive reappraisal (reappraise/negative) and an uninstructed look condition, using static visual images (IAPS). Participants were healthy adults (N=30) with no reported psychiatric/medical history. The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (reappraise > look) and other task contrasts, and describes group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM/FSL) with AlphaSim FWE correction and tables of peak voxels/local maxima referenced for results. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10 and I11. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study must be excluded because the regulated stimuli are dynamic film/video clips (not static visual images), so it fails inclusion criterion I7. Additionally, the article’s reported results focus on seed-based PPI connectivity analyses and does not present a group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation map (with peak coordinates for standard reappraisal task contrasts) in the main text, meeting exclusion criterion E6 and failing I10. Satisfied inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (reappraisal used), I8 (healthy adult sample), and I9 (within-task regulation contrasts reported). Unsatisfied inclusion criteria: I7 (static visual stimuli) and I10 (whole-brain task activation map reported). Therefore the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study using a cognitive reappraisal instruction (reappraise vs maintain/look) with static visual images (IAPS) as stimuli. The sample includes a clearly reported control group (combat-exposed controls without PTSD) reported separately. The paper reports within-task contrasts (Reappraise > Maintain) and provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results with peak coordinates (tables/figures) in standard MNI space; amygdala findings also reported with SVC but whole-brain maps are present. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are met. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I5–I11.

This is a task-based fMRI study of healthy adults using reappraisal to regulate emotion elicited by static visual images (I5, I6, I7). The sample includes healthy adult participants (both HP and non-HP screened for Axis-I disorders) and reports relevant within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., reappraisal negative > view negative) with peak coordinates reported in MNI space (I8, I9, I11). However, the authors state that anatomically-defined ROI analyses were used and the statistical thresholding was ROI-based (FWE correction within ROIs). The manuscript does not report a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map or whole-brain-corrected results accompanying the ROI results. Because the paper appears to report only ROI-based results (or small-volume corrected findings) without an accompanying whole-brain map, it meets exclusion criterion E5 and therefore does not satisfy I10 (whole-brain evidence).

This study is excluded because it does not use reappraisal (I6). Instead, the instructed regulation strategy is mindful acceptance (ACCEPT vs REACT), which falls outside the meta-analysis definition of reappraisal (reinterpretation, perspective-taking, distancing). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (stimuli include static visual images—IAPS), I8 (healthy adult sample reported separately), I9 (within-task regulation contrasts reported, e.g., ACCEPT vs REACT for negative images), I10 (group-level whole-brain task analyses with reported peaks/FWE-corrected results), I11 (results/tables/figures describe whole-brain coordinates). Exclusion criteria met: none. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Because failure to meet I6 (use of reappraisal) is sufficient for exclusion, the study must be excluded despite meeting other criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study using reappraisal of static IAPS images with whole-brain analyses and reported peak coordinates (I5, I6, I7, I9, I10, I11 met). However, the study includes a clinical ADHD group and does not report whole-brain, group-level reappraisal contrasts for the healthy control group separately; the reported reappraise>negative-view results are presented as main effects across the combined sample and interaction tests rather than control-only whole-brain maps. Therefore it does not satisfy I8 (results for healthy controls reported separately). No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) are triggered, but failing I8 requires exclusion per review rules.

This study is excluded because, although it is an empirical task-based fMRI study of healthy adults and includes a separate behavioural cognitive reappraisal (CRA) lab task using static IAPS pictures, the reappraisal manipulation was not implemented during fMRI. The fMRI task involved placebo analgesia with painful heat stimuli (not static visual images), and the paper does not report any within-fMRI-task reappraisal contrasts or whole-brain reappraisal activation coordinates. Therefore key inclusion criteria for this review are not met (see list below). Full text appears complete.

This study meets key inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (explicit cognitive reappraisal condition), I7 (static visual image stimuli), I8 (healthy adult sample reported separately), and I9 (within-task contrasts comparing reappraisal and viewing). However, the provided full text does not report peak coordinates for group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps (no tables/coordinate lists shown in the supplied content). Criterion I10 requires that peak coordinates be reported in a standard space; I cannot verify this from the provided material. Although the paper describes whole-brain analyses and notes supplementary data are available, the necessary coordinates are not present in the supplied full text. Therefore it must be excluded for failure to meet I10. No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) are otherwise triggered by the available information.

This study meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (uses reappraisal as regulation strategy), I7 (static visual images; IAPS), I8 (includes a healthy control group reported separately), and I9 (reports reappraise > attend-negative within-task contrasts). However, the provided full text does not report peak coordinates for whole-brain group-level activation maps in a standard space (MNI/Talairach) required by I10. While whole-brain voxelwise analyses and cluster results (cluster extents, regions) are described and images/supplemental material are referenced, no explicit peak coordinates are present in the supplied full text. Coordinates may exist in online supplements or tables not provided here, but based on the available full text I10 is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria from E4–E8 are clearly met. Therefore I must exclude for failure to meet I10 (whole-brain peak coordinates not reported in the supplied text). If the supplementary tables or full tables with coordinates are available, the study could be re-assessed for inclusion.

This article reports a task-based fMRI study using a cognitive reappraisal (regulate) instruction to down-regulate negative emotions elicited by static IAPS images. It includes healthy adult controls with separate within-task (‘regulate’ > ‘experience’) group-level voxelwise analyses and reports peak coordinates in MNI space. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Although this article meets several methodological requirements for the review (task-based fMRI; reappraisal instruction; static visual IAPS images; a within-task regulation contrast), it does not provide the required whole-brain, group-level activation map/peak coordinates specifically for a healthy control group with no reported psychiatric/medical disorders. Study 2 reports whole-brain coordinates only for between-group contrasts (DSH > depression controls) rather than for the control group’s own decrease>look (regulation) contrast. In addition, the available control sample is described as a ‘depression control group’ (and participants were not explicitly screened to be free of psychiatric history), so it is unclear that a clearly healthy adult group (no prior psychiatric/medical/neurological disorders) is available for inclusion. Therefore I exclude this study. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (reappraisal as regulation), I7 (static visual images), I9 (within-task regulation contrast implemented). Inclusion criteria not met: I8 (unclear/no healthy adult group without psychiatric history), I10 (no whole-brain, group-level regulation map/coordinates reported for a healthy control group). Exclusion criteria met: E7 (results primarily reported as between-group contrasts without the necessary whole-brain regulation map for the target healthy group). Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not use reappraisal as the emotion regulation strategy (I6 not met). The experiment uses affect labeling, an implicit/linguistic labeling task, which is conceptually distinct from reappraisal (reinterpretation, perspective-taking, distancing) required by the review. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (stimuli are static visual images—faces), I8 (healthy control group reported separately), I9 (within-task regulation contrast: affect label > gender label), and I10 (group-level peak coordinates reported in standard space; whole-brain main effects noted in Supplementary Table). No exclusion criteria from the provided list apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded solely for failing I6 (reappraisal requirement).

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation employing reappraisal (and distraction) to downregulate emotional responses to static IAPS images in samples including healthy adult controls. It satisfies multiple inclusion criteria (I5: task-based fMRI; I6: reappraisal used; I7: static visual images used; I8: includes healthy adult control groups reported separately; I9: reports within-task contrasts for reappraisal vs view). However, the full text presents an ROI-focused analysis approach (amygdala, OFC, dlPFC, etc.) with family-wise error correction within those ROIs and psychophysiological interaction results; no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level statistical maps with peak coordinates in standard space (MNI/Talairach) are provided in the supplied full text. Because the paper reports primarily ROI-corrected results without accompanying whole-brain coordinate tables or peak coordinates, it meets exclusion criterion E5 (only ROI/partial-coverage results reported without whole-brain map). Therefore it must be excluded from the meta-analysis that requires whole-brain peak coordinates (I10 not met).

All inclusion criteria are met: (I5) This is an event-related, task-based fMRI study; (I6) Participants were trained to use cognitive reappraisal strategies to increase or decrease emotion (reinterpretation/distancing types); (I7) Emotional stimuli were static IAPS pictures; (I8) Sample comprised healthy adult participants (age 61–65) with no neurological illness; (I9) Within-task regulation contrasts (increase vs. attend; decrease vs. attend) are reported; (I10) Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and reported in Talairach space with cluster coordinates/tables; (I11) Results and coordinates are presented in tables/figures. No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided and appears complete. Hence include in the review.

This is a longitudinal task-based fMRI study (n=49) in healthy adults using cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate negative emotion while viewing static visual images. The fMRI paradigm contrasts Reappraisal vs Maintain (within-task regulation contrast) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates (MNI) for prefrontal and other clusters (Table 1) and amygdala ROI coordinates. Childhood poverty study sample screened for no psychiatric/neurological disorders. Methods, results, and discussion are present; full text appears complete. Thus all inclusion criteria are met (I5–I11); no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is excluded because it does not implement reappraisal as the instructed emotion-regulation strategy (I6 not met) and does not report any within-task contrast of explicit reappraisal vs. baseline/maintain (I9 not met). Instead, it uses an emotional word-face Stroop focused on conflict monitoring/resolution (implicit/automatic emotion processing), not explicit reinterpretation/distancing. Criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (static visual image stimuli—faces), I8 (healthy adult control group reported separately), I10 (group-level whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates reported), I11 (coordinates/tables clearly described). No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that implemented an explicit reappraisal emotion-regulation task (I6) using static visual images (IAPS pictures) as regulated stimuli (I7). The sample consists of healthy adults with exclusion of psychiatric/neurological disorders (I8). The authors report within-task regulation contrasts (Reappraise > Maintain) and related analyses (I9). The methods describe group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster correction and report peak coordinates in Talairach space (e.g., amygdala coordinates provided: left −20, −2, −13; right 32, 2, −16), satisfying whole-brain coordinate reporting (I10). The text includes full Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (fulltext_complete). No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) apply. Therefore the paper should be included for extraction of whole-brain reappraisal activation coordinates.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study using reappraisal (distancing) in a healthy adult sample and reports group-level coordinates for regulation contrasts, it does NOT meet criterion I7: the regulated stimuli are monetary cues/outcomes in a monetary incentive delay (MID) task (anticipatory cues, targets, and monetary feedback), not static visual images (e.g., IAPS photographs). Therefore it fails the stimulus criterion required by the review. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I8, I9, I10, I11. Inclusion criterion not met: I7. No exclusion criteria from the list applied.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using cognitive reappraisal to regulate responses to static visual images of food; however, the provided full text does not report peak coordinates from group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses in standard stereotactic space, which is required (I10). Although the authors performed a whole-brain RFX ANOVA and derived fROIs, the manuscript content supplied here lacks tables/figures with Talairach/MNI peak coordinates or explicit coordinate lists. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (reappraisal used), I7 (static visual image stimuli), I8 (healthy adult sample), I9 (within-task regulation contrasts reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I10 (no peak coordinates in provided text). No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) apply based on the supplied content. Because I10 is not satisfied in the provided material, the study must be excluded for this review.

This multimodal MRI study meets all review inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study using a cognitive reappraisal (Regulate vs Maintain) paradigm with static visual images; it includes a healthy adult control group and reports task contrasts related to emotion regulation; and it provides group-level whole-brain results with peak coordinates (e.g., vmPFC x=-10,y=64,z=-18 and extrastriate cortex x=56,y=-72,z=10) in standard MNI space. One-sample activations for each group were computed and used in analyses, and between-group (HC vs OB) Regulate>Maintain contrasts and coordinates are reported. The full text contains methods, results, and figures/tables describing voxelwise maps and coordinates, so the article is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that uses reappraisal strategies (self-detached and self-immersed; includes up- and down-regulation instructions) as the emotion regulation manipulation (I6). Emotional stimuli were static IAPS pictures (I7). A healthy control group is included and reported separately alongside patients (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., detach > attend, immerse > attend) (I9). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are described (cluster-corrected whole-brain results) and peak coordinates are reported (e.g., left IFG −48,20,−4; left amygdala −20,−2,−16), satisfying whole-brain coordinate reporting (I10,I11). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met. Given these points, the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis focused on task-based reappraisal with static visual stimuli and reported whole-brain coordinates.

The study meets inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (reappraisal: ‘Think Objectively’ reappraisal/distancing), I7 (static visual IAPS images), I8 (healthy adult sample), and I9 (within-task reappraise vs watch contrasts feeding the analyses). However it does NOT meet I10: the paper does not report a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map with peak coordinates in standard space. The analyses focus on seed-based gPPI and ROI-based coupling estimates, and while supplementary or previous work is referenced, no whole-brain activation coordinates are presented in the main report. Therefore exclusion criteria E6 (only seed-based/effective connectivity reported without an accompanying whole-brain task activation map) and E5 (ROI/seed-only results without a whole-brain map) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is excluded because it does not implement reappraisal emotion regulation (I6 not met) and does not report a within-task reappraisal regulation contrast (e.g., “reappraise > look”) for the healthy adult sample (I9 not met). The study uses emotion-labeling and gender-labeling tasks (labeling, not reappraisal/distancing with explicit regulation goal). Satisfied inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (static visual stimuli: faces), I8 (healthy adult sample), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps with MNI coordinates reported), I11 (coordinates/tables/figures described). No exclusion criteria from the review were triggered (exclusion criteria applied: []). Full text appears complete and contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false).

Exclusion E5: the study's emotion-regulation-related analyses are ROI-focused and do not provide a whole-brain reappraisal map with peak coordinates. Inclusion met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (stimuli are static visual images—faces), I8 (healthy control group reported separately). Inclusion NOT met: I6 (no reappraisal instruction—participants were told to ignore emotional face distracters rather than use reappraisal/reinterpretation/perspective-taking to modulate their emotion), I9 (no within-task contrast implementing reappraisal such as “reappraise > look”; contrasts examine distracter presence vs absence rather than explicit regulation instructions), I10 (no group-level whole-brain task map with peak coordinates for an explicit reappraisal contrast; regulation-related results are reported as ROI analyses). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study does not meet the review's requirement that emotion regulation be implemented via reappraisal with accompanying whole-brain coordinates.

This is a task-based fMRI study using cognitive reappraisal (detach/experience) to down-regulate/up-regulate emotion to static visual IAPS images. Participants are healthy adults (both younger and older samples reported separately). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., Positive-Regulate > Positive-Experience; Negative-Regulate > Negative-Experience) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates in MNI space (cluster-corrected maps and coordinate tables/figures). Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I10 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study meets multiple inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5), uses reappraisal as an emotion-regulation strategy (I6), employs static visual images from the IAPS (I7), includes a healthy control group reported separately (I8), and reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., reappraise > attend negative) (I9). However, the provided full text does not contain peak activation coordinates in a standard reference space (MNI or Talairach) or a table listing whole-brain peak coordinates; placeholders in the results suggest coordinates/tables/figures are omitted. Therefore I10 (group-level whole-brain peak coordinates reported) cannot be confirmed from the provided content. No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) are triggered. Because the meta-analysis requires reported whole-brain peak coordinates (I10), this record must be excluded based on the available text.

Excluded because the study enrolled only patients with social anxiety disorder and did not report a separate healthy adult control group (fails I8). Additionally, the neuroimaging analyses focused on a priori ROI-based tests and did not report a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map with peak coordinates (fails I10), which also invokes exclusion criterion E5 (only ROI analyses reported without an accompanying whole-brain map). The study does meet several inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (explicit reappraisal task: Reappraise vs Maintain), I7 (static visual images/IAPS), and I9 (within-task regulation contrasts reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I8 and I10. Therefore the paper is not eligible for inclusion in this meta-analysis.

This study meets several inclusion criteria for the review (I5: task-based fMRI; I6: reappraisal used as the regulation strategy—REAPPRAISE; I7: regulated stimuli are static visual images from IAPS; I9: reports a within-task regulation contrast REAPPRAISE-Negative > LOOK-Negative; I10: reports group-level whole-brain task activation maps with peak coordinates in standard space; I11: coordinates/results are presented in tables/figures). However, it fails I8 (Target sample): the participant group consists solely of individuals with Alcohol Use Disorder (clinical sample) and no healthy control group results are reported separately. No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) are triggered. Therefore the study must be excluded from this meta-analysis because it lacks a healthy adult sample or separable healthy control data.

This is a task-based fMRI study that used instructed reappraisal (reinterpretation) of negative IAPS pictures (static visual images) in a healthy adult sample (N=18). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (Reappraise > Negative, Negative > Reappraise) and confirms whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with FDR correction; peak coordinates are reported in tables (e.g., Table 1 and Table 2) in standard space. Although ROI analyses were also performed, whole-brain results are provided. All inclusion criteria for the review (I5–I11) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using static visual images (I7) and reports whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates (I10/I11). However, it does NOT use reappraisal (or reinterpretation/perspective-taking/distancing with an explicit regulation goal) as the emotion regulation strategy — it uses an affective Stroop distraction task (violates I6). The sample is children/adolescents with ADHD and healthy youth, not healthy adults (violates I8). The study does not report any within-task reappraisal contrasts (e.g., reappraise > look) for a healthy adult group (violates I9). No exclusion criteria from the list (E4–E8) are specifically met. Therefore the study must be excluded.

Full text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI with an emotion regulation task), I6 (explicit reappraisal-style instructions to ‘increase’ or ‘decrease’ emotional responses), I7 (static visual stimuli: IAPS pictures), I9 (within-task contrasts reported: increase>attend and decrease>attend), I10 (group-level voxelwise analyses with reported MNI coordinates), I11 (coordinates/tables/figures reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I8 (target sample criterion). The sample includes participants with lifetime history of depressive disorder and current symptoms; the paper does not report results for a separate healthy-only control group nor restrict analyses to a clearly defined healthy adult group without psychiatric history. No exclusion criteria from the review (E4–E8) are directly triggered by the report. Because the review requires at least one group of healthy adults reported separately (I8) and this study does not provide a healthy-only group-level activation map, it cannot be included in the meta-analysis.

This study does not implement or instruct reappraisal (reinterpretation/perspective-taking/distancing) as an emotion regulation strategy; instead it examines pain as an affect-regulation mechanism in BPD. No within-task reappraisal contrasts (e.g., “reappraise > look”) are reported for any group. Although the study is a task-based fMRI study using static visual images and includes a healthy control group, it does not report group-level whole-brain task maps for a reappraisal/regulation contrast. Therefore it fails the key inclusion criteria required for this meta-analysis.

The full text describes a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants using cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate craving for appetitive stimuli (personalized food images). Stimuli were static visual images shown during scanning. Behavioral and whole-brain univariate and multivariate fMRI analyses are reported, including group-level voxelwise contrasts (e.g., regulate > look, look > regulate) with tables of regions and MNI coordinates and cluster statistics. Thus the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review (task-based fMRI; reappraisal strategy; static visual images; healthy adult sample; within-task regulation contrasts reported; whole-brain group-level results with coordinates). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is excluded because it does not meet I8: the healthy control sample is a mixed adolescent/adult sample (ages 12.1–29.5) and the paper does not report results for an adult-only healthy group separately; the review requires at least one healthy adult group. The study does satisfy other inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (reappraisal via distancing), I7 (static visual images—IAPS/Emopics), I9 (within-task regulation contrasts reported: positive watch vs positive distance), I10 (whole-brain analyses performed and reported in supplementary tables/figures with coordinates), and I11 (reporting in supplement is acceptable). No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) are triggered. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This study examines distraction (a working-memory based attentional diversion) rather than reappraisal/distancing as the regulation strategy. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (static visual images—IAPS), I8 (includes a healthy trauma-exposed control group reported separately), I9 (reports a within-task regulation contrast: distract-negative > attend-negative). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (does not use reappraisal or its listed variants—distraction is a different strategy), I10 (no clear whole-brain group-level reappraisal contrast with peak coordinates reported for the healthy control group specifically). No exclusion criteria from the review (E4–E8) are met. Therefore the study is ineligible for the reappraisal-focused meta-analysis because the regulated strategy is distraction rather than reappraisal/distancing, and requisite whole-brain reappraisal contrast for healthy adults is absent.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using static visual images and reports within-task contrasts and group-level peak coordinates, it does not implement reappraisal (reinterpretation/perspective-taking/distancing) as the instructed emotion regulation strategy. The task is affect labeling (naming emotion labels), an incidental labeling procedure rather than an explicit reappraisal/regulate instruction. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 (reappraisal). All other inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (static visual images), I8 (healthy adult sample reported separately), I9 (within-task regulation-related contrast reported), I10 (group-level whole-brain peaks reported). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text appears complete.

This study uses an fMRI approach-avoidance (AA) task assessing control over automatic action tendencies to emotional faces, not a reappraisal instruction (reinterpretation, perspective-taking, or distancing). Although it is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults, uses static visual stimuli (faces), reports within-task regulation contrasts (incongruent > congruent), and provides whole-brain coordinates, it does not implement or instruct reappraisal as the emotion regulation strategy. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (reappraisal strategy) is not met. Full text appears complete.

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation using a cognitive reappraisal task (explicit downregulation and upregulation instructions) with static visual images from the IAPS. Participants were healthy adult volunteers (female students) with no reported psychiatric or neurological disorders. The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to reappraisal (e.g., downregulate negative > attend negative, attend negative > attend neutral) and conducts group-level, whole-brain second-level analyses (SPM normalization to MNI space); the authors state that t-maps and con images of second-level whole-brain analyses are provided in the Supporting Information and describe whole-brain clusters in standard space. The methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

(a) Exclusion criteria met: E6 — the study reports only resting-state (seed-based) functional connectivity analyses (amygdala RSFC) without any task-evoked whole-brain activation maps. (b) Inclusion criteria met: none. (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not a task-based fMRI study), I6 (does not use reappraisal or any explicit emotion-regulation task), I7 (no static visual emotional stimuli; resting-state with eyes-open black screen), I8 (sample is methamphetamine-dependent adults, not healthy controls), I9 (no within-task regulation contrasts reported), I10 (no whole-brain task-evoked peak coordinates in standard space). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the paper does not address the meta-analysis objective and is excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that explicitly used reappraisal instructions for down-regulation (I6), tested a healthy adult, population-derived sample (I8), and reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., regulate negative > watch negative) (I9). However, the emotional stimuli were 30-second film/video clips rather than static visual images, violating inclusion criterion I7 (stimuli must be static images). Additionally, the provided text does not clearly report peak coordinates for whole-brain task activation maps in standard space for the regulation contrasts (I10 not met based on provided content). Therefore the study must be excluded for not meeting I7 (and I10 based on available text). No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) are applicable.

This study is a resting-state fMRI experiment that administered an acute tryptophan depletion challenge; it does not implement any task-based emotion regulation paradigm. Inclusion met: I8 (healthy adult sample). Inclusion not met: I5 (not a task-based fMRI study), I6 (no reappraisal or instructed regulation), I7 (no regulation of static visual stimuli; resting state, no stimulus presentation), I9 (no within-task regulation contrasts reported), I10 (no whole-brain task-evoked activation maps/coordinates). Exclusion criteria met: E6 (reports only resting-state analyses without any task activation maps). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. It is a task-based fMRI study (I5) in which participants used a reappraisal/distancing strategy (labelled ‘reappraise’ and described as adopting a detached/unemotional attitude) as an emotion regulation instruction (I6). The regulated stimuli were static visual images drawn from the IAPS (I7). The sample comprised healthy adult participants with exclusion of psychiatric/neurological disorders (I8). The authors report within-task contrasts comparing regulation versus attend (e.g., ER > attend and attend > ER) at the group level (I9). Whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and the manuscript indicates conversion/reporting of peak coordinates in standard space and presents whole-brain results (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria are met: the paper reports whole-brain task activation maps (not ROI-only or connectivity-only), includes within-task contrasts rather than only between-group comparisons, and includes explicit regulation instructions (so not an empathy-only task). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, figures/tables referenced).

Meets all inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI using cognitive reappraisal (reframing/distancing) to increase/decrease emotion (I6); stimuli are static IAPS images (I7); includes a healthy control group reported separately (I8); reports within-task contrasts (increase>maintain, decrease>maintain) (I9); whole-brain voxelwise SPM8 analyses with cluster correction and peak coordinates reported (e.g., right amygdala 20 -6 20) satisfying group-level whole-brain coordinate reporting (I10); clearly a task-based fMRI study (I5). Full text is complete. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of emotional picture processing with healthy control subjects (I5, I7, I8 satisfied) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster coordinates (I10 satisfied). However, the task is a passive picture-viewing/expectation paradigm with no instruction to reappraise, reinterpret, or otherwise regulate emotion, and no within-task reappraisal contrasts (e.g., “reappraise > look”, “down-regulate > maintain”) are reported. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 (use of reappraisal as the regulation strategy) and I9 (reporting at least one within-task regulation contrast) are not met. No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) apply. Full text appears complete.

Excluded because the study does not meet key inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that includes a healthy control group (I8) and reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (anger-distraction vs anger-engagement) (I9). However, the regulation strategy implemented is distraction (instructing participants to 'distract themselves'), not reappraisal (reinterpretation, perspective-taking, or distancing) as required (I6 not met). Critically, the emotional stimuli are audiotaped narrative stories (audio), not static visual images such as IAPS pictures or photographs (I7 not met). Additionally, the provided full text does not present whole-brain peak coordinates in standard space in the excerpt (I10 not met). No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) are triggered based on the provided text. Therefore the study is ineligible for inclusion.

The study manipulated cognitive distraction (0-back vs 2-back) during anticipation of negative/neutral pictures — an attentional distraction task — rather than using reappraisal (reinterpretation, distancing, or perspective-taking) as the instructed regulation strategy. Therefore it does not meet I6. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (regulated stimuli were static visual images, IAPS), I8 (healthy adult sample reported separately), I9 (reports within-task contrasts related to regulation via distraction), I10 (group-level whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates reported), I11 (whole-brain results described). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (reappraisal). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study of script-driven imagery (auditory narratives and imagined aggressive scenarios) in BPD and healthy women, but it does NOT use reappraisal as an emotion-regulation strategy nor instruct participants to regulate their emotion. The regulated stimuli are narrative scripts and imagined scenarios (not static visual images). The analyses focus on task-dependent whole-brain functional connectivity differences (network/component statistics), not on within-task reappraisal contrasts (e.g., reappraise > look) or whole-brain voxelwise activation peak coordinates. Therefore it fails to meet key inclusion criteria (I6, I7, I9, I10). It does include a task (I5) and reports a healthy control group (I8), but does not provide the required reappraisal-based, whole-brain activation contrasts for healthy adults.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study with static visual stimuli (partner facial photographs) in a healthy adult sample and reports group-level activation coordinates, it does NOT implement an instructed reappraisal (or other explicit emotion regulation) task nor report a within-task reappraisal-related contrast (e.g., reappraise > look). The fMRI task explicitly stated there were no instructions to regulate emotional reactions, and reported contrasts are stimulus valence contrasts (partner negative vs neutral, etc.), not regulation contrasts. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 (use of reappraisal/regulation strategy) and I9 (reports within-task regulation contrast). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8. Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6, I9 (also I10 is debatable but not required given the above failures). No exclusion criteria from the list directly apply.

Full text shows a task-based fMRI experiment in healthy adults with group-level whole-brain contrasts and reported coordinates, but it does NOT meet key review requirements: (1) the emotion-regulation strategy is thought suppression (instructions to 'don't think'), not reappraisal (reinterpretation/perspective-taking/distancing with an explicit regulation goal), and (2) the emotional material consists of imagined/remembered relationship scenarios (internally generated/imagined stimuli), not static visual images (e.g., IAPS pictures or photographs). Therefore the study fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7, though it meets I5, I8, I9, I10, and I11. No exclusion criteria from the review (E4–E8) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study using static visual images (faces and bodies) with healthy control and clinical groups, and it reports whole-brain voxelwise results. However, participants were not instructed to use reappraisal or any emotion-regulation strategy; the task involved passive viewing and occasional attractiveness ratings. No within-task emotion-regulation contrasts (e.g., reappraise > look, down-regulate > maintain) are reported. Therefore the study fails key inclusion criteria I6 (use of reappraisal/regulation strategy) and I9 (reports regulation-related within-task contrasts). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (static visual stimuli), I8 (healthy adult control group reported separately), I10 (whole-brain group-level maps with peak coordinates). No exclusion criteria from the review (E4–E8) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not implement reappraisal-based emotion regulation nor use static visual image stimuli. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (healthy adult control group reported separately), I10 (group-level whole-brain maps with peak coordinates reported in MNI space), I11 (coordinates/tables/figures clearly described). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no reappraisal/reinterpretation/distancing manipulation — study used guided individualized imagery of stress and alcohol-cue), I7 (stimuli are auditory-guided autobiographical imagery scripts, not static visual images), I9 (no within-task contrast of an explicit regulation condition, e.g., reappraise > look; contrasts are exposure-based such as stress > neutral). No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) were specifically triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Excluded because the study does not implement reappraisal-based emotion regulation (I6 not met). The in-scanner task involved viewing self-referential emotional statements and rating emotion intensity without instructions to reinterpret, distance, or otherwise regulate affect. The stimuli are verbal/self-referential statements rather than static visual images (I7 not met). The paper does not report a within-task emotion-regulation contrast (e.g., reappraise>look) for the healthy adult sample (I9 not met), nor are whole-brain peak coordinates reported for any regulation contrast in standard space (I10 not met). Inclusion criteria satisfied: I5 (task-based fMRI study) and I8 (healthy adult participants). No exclusion criteria from the provided list apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using explicit cognitive reappraisal instructions (reappraise vs attend) to regulate emotional responses to static visual images (IAPS and validated alcohol photographs). The sample includes a healthy control group reported separately alongside alcohol-dependent patients. The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts ([reappraise > attend] per emotion) and second-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (results reported at whole-brain p<0.05 FWE; peak coordinates and tables/figures are provided). All inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

The study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: I6 (emotion regulation strategy = reappraisal) is not met — the task uses affect labeling, not reappraisal/perspective-taking/distancing with an explicit regulation goal; I7 (stimuli are static visual images) is not met — stimuli are dynamic video clips of adolescent faces; I8 (target sample = healthy adults) is not met — sample is a cross-sectional adolescent female sample (ages 10–23) without a separate adult-only group reported. Inclusion criteria that are met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I9 (reports a within-task regulation-related contrast: Label > Blur and Label > View), I10 (group-level whole-brain analyses with reported coordinates and NeuroVault maps), and I11 (results clearly described/available). No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI experiment in healthy adults that uses instructed cognitive reappraisal (decrease) to regulate responses to static visual images (IAPS). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (decrease negative > look negative and inverse) and whole-brain group-level voxelwise results with peak coordinates in standard space (SPM-normalized; multiple tables/figures list coordinates). The sample are healthy adults with exclusions for psychiatric/neurological conditions. No exclusion criteria are met: whole-brain analyses are reported (not only ROI), results include task activation contrasts (not only connectivity or between-group-only comparisons), and the study is empirical with original data. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; fulltext_incomplete set to false.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study using a cognitive reappraisal instruction (reappraise vs attend) to down-regulate negative emotion, with static visual stimuli drawn from the IAPS. A healthy control group (n=16) is reported separately. The analyses include within-task contrasts (Reappraisal > Attend Negative) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistics, with peak coordinates reported (e.g., MNI coords −44,26,12).
