Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment that used cognitive reappraisal and reports whole-brain, group-level Reappraise vs React contrasts with peak coordinates for healthy controls. However, it does not meet the stimulus criterion required by the review: the regulated stimuli are not strictly static visual images. Of the three tasks, two use dynamic video clips (Criticism) or autobiographical text (Beliefs), and the Faces task—although based on photographs—presented faces with an apparent looming/motion effect across the trial (dynamic presentation). Because the emotional stimuli are not static images as required by I7, the study does not qualify for inclusion despite meeting other criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using detachment (a distancing/perspective-taking form of reappraisal) to down-regulate emotion while viewing static visual images (IAPS and EmoPicS). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., Negative Permit > Negative Detach and vice versa) computed at the group level with whole-brain, voxelwise second-level one-sample t-tests (thresholded, FWE corrected) and provides peak coordinates (e.g., amygdala peaks and other regions). The sample comprises healthy adults with separate reporting of relevant within-group results. Full text includes methods, results (with coordinates), and discussion. All required inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10,I11) are met. No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study using explicit reappraisal of static visual images and includes healthy control participants and reappraise>attend contrasts, but the provided full text does not report any whole-brain peak coordinates (MNI/Talairach) for the reappraisal/regulation contrasts. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (reappraisal task), I7 (static visual image stimuli), I8 (healthy control group reported separately), I9 (within-task reappraise>attend contrasts computed). Inclusion criteria not met: I10 (no whole-brain peak coordinates reported in provided text), I11 (no coordinates/tables of whole-brain results provided). No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) are triggered based on the provided content.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that used cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate negative emotion elicited by static visual images (IAPS). The methods describe a within-task contrast (Reappraise > Maintain) analyzed at the group level, and the paper reports group-level voxelwise results with peak coordinates (e.g., left amygdala [−22,0,−22] and PPI cluster coordinates in Table 1). Although the emphasis is on psychophysiological interaction (seed-based connectivity), the paper also includes whole-brain group analyses (conjunction and PPI maps) with reported coordinates, meeting the review’s requirement for whole-brain coordinates. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

Excluded because the study used dynamic film/video clips as stimuli rather than static visual images (violates inclusion criterion I7). Additionally, the reported analyses were restricted to an a priori PFC–amygdala mask (small-volume/masked approach) rather than a whole-brain voxelwise group activation map, which meets exclusion criterion E5 and means inclusion criterion I10 (whole-brain group-level map with coordinates) is not satisfied. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (reappraisal used as a regulation strategy), I8 (healthy adult sample reported separately), I9 (within-task regulation contrasts reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (stimuli are films/videos, not static images), I10 (no whole-brain group-level task activation map; analyses limited to masked/ROI search space). Full text appears complete.

The study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for the review. It is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (I5 and I8 satisfied). However, the emotional stimuli were film/video clips (dynamic visual stimuli), not static images, so I7 (static visual stimuli) is not met. The task was a non-directive passive viewing of emotional clips with no instruction to reappraise or use reinterpretation/perspective-taking/distancing, so I6 (use of reappraisal strategy) is not met. The reported contrasts compare emotion-evoking vs neutral clips (EE − EN) and group differences; there is no within-task reappraisal contrast (e.g., reappraise > look), so I9 (within-task regulation contrast) is not met. Finally, although whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted, the provided full text does not present peak coordinates in standard space for regulation contrasts, so I10 cannot be confirmed from the available text. Therefore the study does not satisfy required criteria and is excluded.

The study is a task-based fMRI study of reappraisal in healthy adults (I5, I6, I8). However, it does not meet key inclusion requirements: the regulated stimuli are not static visual images but a social/behavioral task (Taylor Aggression Paradigm) with auditory white-noise punishments, so I7 (static visual stimuli) is not met. The provided full text does not report peak coordinates in standard space for whole-brain maps (no Talairach/MNI coordinates/tables visible), so I10 is not met. Furthermore, the reappraisal manipulation is implemented as a between-subjects instruction (Reappraisal vs Control), and the reported regulation-related results are between-group contrasts rather than within-task reappraise>look contrasts, which falls under exclusion criterion E7. Although task contrasts and group effects are reported (I9 satisfied), failure to meet I7 and I10 (and presence of E7) requires exclusion.

Full text meets all inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI with explicit reappraisal instructions (down-regulation/distancing), regulated stimuli are static visual images (IAPS and in-house pictures), participants are healthy adults, within-task regulation contrasts are reported (e.g., reappraise > view, reappraise > suppress), and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with MNI coordinates and thresholding are described and reported. The full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (fulltext appears complete). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and the perspective-taking instruction included an explicit regulation goal).

This study is excluded because the sample consists of patients with spider phobia and no healthy adult control group is reported, so it does not meet I8 (target sample: healthy adults). Met inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (reappraisal used as the regulation strategy), I7 (stimuli were static visual images — spider photographs), I9 (within-task regulation contrasts reported: regulate vs watch), and I10 (whole-brain random-effects analyses with results reported and data normalized to Talairach space; supplementary coordinates/tables referenced). No exclusion criteria from the review (E4–E8) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that explicitly implements cognitive reappraisal (down-regulation) as one condition (I6); the regulated stimuli are static visual images from the IAPS (I7); the sample comprises healthy adult participants with exclusion of psychiatric/medical conditions and separate reporting for controls (I8); within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., Reappraise > Observe; Label > Observe) are reported (I9); group-level voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates in standard space (MNI) are presented for whole-brain results (I10), and results/tables/figures clearly describe whole-brain coordinates (I11). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study using a distancing reappraisal strategy with healthy adult participants and reports within-task, group-level whole-brain activation contrasts with coordinates (satisfies I5, I6, I8, I9, I10). However, the emotional stimulus in the task is anticipatory threat of painful electric shock (instructed fear/anticipatory anxiety) and auditory cues—NOT static visual images (e.g., IAPS photos). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I7 (stimuli must be static visual images). No exclusion criteria from the list (E4–E8) are triggered by the full text. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because the regulated emotional stimuli are autobiographical memory recall (participants recalled sad autobiographical events, listened to sad music, and used brief visual reminder phrases) rather than static visual images. This violates inclusion criterion I7 (excludes imagined/ recalled autobiographical scenarios). The paper does meet multiple other inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (reappraisal used as an ER strategy), I8 (healthy adult sample reported separately), I9 (within-task contrast reported, e.g., reappraisal > fixation), and I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates reported). No exclusion criteria E4–E8 are otherwise triggered by the full text. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports a task-based fMRI investigation (ERT) that explicitly uses cognitive reappraisal (Reappraise > Maintain) to down-regulate emotion in healthy adult participants. The regulated stimuli are static visual IAPS images. The sample is healthy adults with no psychiatric diagnoses reported. The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (Reappraise > Maintain) and describes voxelwise whole-brain thresholding for that contrast, and provides peak coordinates for emotion-regulatory clusters (e.g., left DLPFC x,y,z = −40,12,28 and VLPFC sphere at −50,22,6), satisfying the requirement for group-level whole-brain peak coordinates. While some follow-up analyses used ROI-extracted betas, whole-brain voxelwise results and peak coordinates are reported for the relevant reappraisal contrast. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5–I10 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study using cognitive reappraisal (Regulate vs Attend) with static visual stimuli (conditioned colored squares and cigarette pictures) and reports within-task contrasts. However, the participant sample consists solely of nicotine-dependent smokers (no healthy adult control group reported separately), so it does not meet the requirement that the target sample include healthy adults (I8). Additionally, the provided full text does not report peak whole-brain coordinates in standard space that would confirm I10. Therefore the study must be excluded for failure to meet I8 (and I10 not confirmed).

Excluded because the emotional stimuli regulated were narrative scripts with script-driven mental imagery (imagined scenarios), not static visual images — thus failing inclusion criterion I7. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (reappraisal/perspective-taking used as regulation strategy), I8 (healthy adult sample), I9 (within-task regulation contrasts reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (stimuli are not static visual images; they are narratives/imagined scenarios), and I10 (uncertain/non-evident reporting of peak coordinates in standard space in the provided full text). No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) directly applied based on the provided full text. Full text appears complete for screening.

Full text reports a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=24) using explicit emotion regulation. Reappraisal (cognitive distancing) was one of two instructed strategies. Emotional stimuli were static IAPS images. The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., regulate > maintain; increase > decrease) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses conducted in SPM8 with peak coordinates in MNI space (e.g., amygdala and dorsomedial PFC coordinates). All inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

Excluded because the study sample consists exclusively of clinical patients (anxious and/or depressed adults) and no separate healthy control group or healthy-adult results are reported, so inclusion criterion I8 (target sample: healthy adults reported separately) is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (reappraisal as regulation strategy), I7 (static visual images used as stimuli), I9 (within-task regulation contrast Reappraise > Maintain reported), I10 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates reported), I11 (results and coordinates clearly described). Inclusion criteria not met: I8 (no healthy adult group/results reported separately). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study is excluded because the emotional stimuli being regulated are socio-economic game offers (Dictator Game monetary/social decision outcomes), which do not satisfy inclusion criterion I7 (the review excludes studies where regulated stimuli are monetary or social decision outcomes rather than static visual images). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (reappraisal/mentalizing strategy used), I8 (healthy adult sample reported), I9 (within-task regulation contrasts reported, e.g., DOWN>LOOK, UP>LOOK), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported with thresholding), and I11 (peak coordinates/tables reported). Exclusion criteria met: none of E4–E8 apply. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not implement reappraisal or an explicit emotion-regulation instruction. Regulation of emotion is implicit (manipulated via financial incentive context) rather than an instructed reappraisal strategy, so inclusion criteria I6 (reappraisal used as the regulation strategy) is not met. Consequently, there is no within-task reappraisal/regulation contrast such as “reappraise > look” or equivalent, so I9 is not met. The study does meet several other inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (stimuli are static visual images—faces), I8 (healthy adult sample reported separately), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps with peak coordinates reported), and I11 (coordinates/tables/figures provided). The exclusion criterion E8 applies because this is an empathy/perspective-taking context without explicit instruction to amplify or attenuate participants’ own emotional responses (the manipulation is contextual/incentive-based rather than instructed reappraisal). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I10, I11. Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I9. Exclusion criteria applied: E8.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that includes an explicit reappraisal training/condition used during the fMRI task. Stimuli were static visual images (IAPS photographs). The authors report within-task contrasts derived from the Regulation condition (Negative vs Neutral during Regulate trials) and conduct whole-brain voxelwise analyses, reporting peak MNI coordinates for a significant cluster (right AI/OFC peak [24,26,-8]). The sample includes healthy adult participants and results for the task/regulation conditions are reported at the group level. The full text contains Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment using cognitive reappraisal (psychological distancing) with static visual IAPS social images (I5,I6,I7). It includes a healthy adult control group reported separately (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., Reappraise Negative > Look Negative) and analyzes reappraisal implementation and anticipation (I9). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and peak coordinates are reported in MNI space in the text/tables/supplement (I10,I11). Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., whole-brain maps are reported, not ROI-only; not connectivity/resting-state-only; not non-empirical). Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study using cognitive reappraisal (decrease) during an emotion regulation paradigm with static IAPS images in a healthy adult community sample. The paper reports within-task contrasts for regulation (regulate negative > look negative) and provides whole-brain group-level results with peak MNI coordinates (mPFC, dlPFC, IPC) and correction thresholds. Full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion. Thus all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI experiment (I5) that instructs participants to use cognitive reappraisal (reinterpretation) to down-regulate negative emotion (I6). The regulated stimuli were static visual IAPS images (I7). The sample comprises healthy adult volunteers with screening for psychiatric/neurological history (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., RU–CU, (CU–CN)–(RU–RN)) (I9). Analyses were whole-brain random-effects voxelwise maps with peak coordinates reported (MNI/Talairach coordinates are provided for amygdala, insula, PFC clusters) (I10), described in the text and figures (I11). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, not between-group-only, etc.). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore, include for the meta-analysis.

This full-text reports a within-subjects task-based fMRI study using cognitive reappraisal (explicit upregulate and downregulate instructions) with static IAPS images, in healthy adult participants (younger and older groups). It presents task contrasts of interest (downregulate > maintain, upregulate > maintain, negative > neutral) and reports whole-brain analyses (thresholded maps; results and coordinate tables referenced in supplementary material and NeuroVault). Thus all inclusion criteria are met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (reappraisal strategy), I7 (static visual IAPS stimuli), I8 (healthy adult sample with separable groups), I9 (within-task regulation contrasts reported), I10 (group-level whole-brain maps with peak coordinates reported in supplements/NeuroVault), and I11 (results available in supplemental/tables). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is excluded because it does not implement or report a reappraisal (emotion-regulation) contrast for healthy adults. Although it is a task-based fMRI study with a healthy control group reported separately (I5 and I8 satisfied), the manuscript only reports React (natural viewing) versus Asterisks contrasts; the Reframe/regulation condition is mentioned but not analyzed or reported here. Therefore the paper does not meet required criteria for (a) use of reappraisal/emotion-regulation as the relevant task (I6), (b) regulation-related within-task contrasts reported (I9), (c) whole-brain group-level regulation maps/peak coordinates for the regulation contrast (I10). Additionally, the stimuli that would be regulated include dynamic videos and participant-generated sentences (Criticism, Beliefs), which do not meet the static visual-image stimulus requirement (I7). No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) are triggered by the report itself. Full text appears complete.

Excluded because inclusion criterion I7 is not met: the study regulated emotional responses to short video clips (dynamic film stimuli and embedded videos of a person) rather than static visual images. The study does meet other inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (reappraisal used as an emotion regulation strategy, alongside suppression), I8 (healthy adult sample reported), I9 (within-task regulation contrasts such as reappraise > watch are reported), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates reported), and I11 (coordinates/tables/figures described). No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not implement reappraisal-based emotion regulation and does not report whole-brain task activation coordinates. Specifically, regulation was achieved via recall of autobiographical memories (imagined/remembered scenarios) rather than reappraisal (I6 not met), and the regulated stimuli during regulation blocks were recalled AMs (excluded by I7). The manuscript reports primarily ROI-based task analyses (beta weights from hippocampus/intraparietal sulcus) and resting-state ReHo/ALFF results, with no clear whole-brain, voxelwise task activation maps with peak coordinates reported (I10 not met). It does meet that it is a task-based fMRI study (I5), includes healthy adult participants (I8), and reports within-task regulation contrasts (I9). Exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only task results / no accompanying whole-brain task map) applies.

Excluded because the study does not meet inclusion criterion I6 (use of reappraisal). Although the paper is a task-based fMRI experiment (I5) using static visual images (I7) in a healthy adult sample (I8), reports within-task regulation contrasts (REGULATE vs VIEW) (I9), and includes whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates reported in standard space (I10), the emotion regulation manipulation was neurofeedback-driven (instructed to ‘regulate the feeling center’) without explicit instruction to use reappraisal strategies (reinterpretation, perspective-taking, or distancing). Therefore I6 is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports whole-brain group-level coordinate results, but it does NOT use reappraisal/instructional emotion regulation: participants played a violent video game (dynamic stimuli) rather than performing reappraisal, reinterpretation, distancing, or perspective-taking with an explicit regulation goal. Stimuli are dynamic/interactive video game sessions (not static images). The reported analyses focus on seed-based task-dependent functional connectivity (amygdala connectivity) rather than conventional whole-brain task activation contrasts of an emotion regulation contrast (e.g., reappraise > look). Therefore the study fails inclusion criteria I6 (reappraisal), I7 (static visual stimuli), and I9 (within-task emotion-regulation contrasts), and it meets exclusion criterion E6 (reports only seed-based connectivity without a whole-brain task activation map). Full text appears complete.

This study does not meet the review’s core requirement of using reappraisal as the emotion-regulation strategy (Inclusion I6). The task is an implicit emotional-interference (attend vs ignore) paradigm rather than explicit reappraisal/distancing/reinterpretation. Although it is a task-based fMRI study (I5), uses static visual stimuli (faces/houses) (I7), and includes a healthy control group reported separately (I8), it fails to implement or contrast reappraisal instructions (I6) and does not report an explicit reappraisal-related within-task contrast (I9). Additionally, analyses were conducted within a priori and exploratory ROI masks rather than reporting a whole-brain, voxelwise group-level map (I10), so the paper appears to provide ROI-constrained results only (Exclusion E5). Therefore it is not eligible for inclusion in this meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that used an explicit reappraisal (reappraise) emotion-regulation instruction (I6) during a positive emotion regulation task with static IAPS images (I7). Neuroimaging analyses include within-task contrasts for emotion regulation (reappraise > view) entered into group-level tests (I9). However, the sample consists entirely of nicotine-dependent smokers (a clinical/substance-use population) with no separate healthy control group reported, so the target-sample criterion for healthy adults is not met (I8 not satisfied). Additionally, the provided full text does not report peak coordinates from whole-brain, group-level task activation maps in a standard space (Talairach/MNI), which is required (I10 not satisfied). No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) appear to be violated. Because two required inclusion criteria (I8 and I10) are not met, the study must be excluded.

The study is excluded because it does not implement reappraisal or an explicit emotion-regulation instruction: the fMRI task is affect labeling (choosing labels for facial expressions), not reinterpretation/perspective-taking/distancing aimed at changing one’s emotional response (I6 not met). Consequently, there are no within-task reappraisal/regulation contrasts (e.g., “reappraise > look”) reported for the target sample (I9 not met). The full text is complete and provides methods, results, and coordinates. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (static visual stimuli — photographs of faces), I8 (includes a healthy adult control group reported separately), and I10 (group-level whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates reported in MNI). No exclusion criteria from the review (E4–E8) are triggered. Therefore the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria (notably I6 and I9) and must be excluded.

The study does not meet several key inclusion criteria for the review. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no reappraisal or explicit emotion-regulation instruction — participants simply viewed mother/child play vs separation), I7 (stimuli are dynamic video clips, not static visual images), I9 (no within-task contrast that indexes an explicit regulation instruction such as “reappraise > look”), I10 (no peak whole-brain coordinates reported in the provided text; whole-brain cluster results are described but coordinates/tables are not present in the full text provided). Exclusion criteria met: none of E4–E8 apply. Because multiple required inclusion criteria (I6, I7, I9, and likely I10) are not satisfied, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

Excluded because the study does not implement reappraisal-based emotion regulation (I6 not met) and does not report a within-task reappraisal contrast (I9 not met) or whole-brain peak coordinates from a voxelwise group map (I10 not met). The task is an emotional-distractor n-back in which participants are instructed to ignore emotional faces (an attentional-distraction paradigm), not to reinterpret, reappraise, or explicitly up-/down-regulate emotion. Analyses were conducted as ROI-based second-level models (region-of-interest approach) rather than reporting whole-brain voxelwise peak coordinates (exclusion E5 applies). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (static visual face stimuli), I8 (healthy adult control group reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (reappraisal strategy), I9 (within-task reappraisal regulation contrast), I10 (whole-brain coordinates reported). Full text appears complete.

This study is an RCT of Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction in fibromyalgia patients with neuroimaging (resting-state fMRI, pCASL), structural MRI (VBM, DTI) and inflammatory markers. It does not implement a task-based emotion regulation (reappraisal) paradigm or report within-task emotion regulation contrasts or task-evoked whole-brain activation coordinates. The sample is a clinical FMS patient group (not healthy adults). Thus it fails the meta-analysis inclusion criteria: no task-based reappraisal (I5,I6), stimuli are not task static emotional images within a reappraisal task (I7), target sample is not healthy adults (I8), no within-task regulation contrasts reported (I9), and no whole-brain task activation coordinates provided (I10). Exclusion criteria met: E6 (reports resting-state and perfusion/structural imaging but no whole-brain task-evoked activation maps for reappraisal). Inclusion criteria met: none.

This study is excluded because it is a PET study of endogenous opioid responses to self-induced sadness and does not implement reappraisal of static visual stimuli in a task-based fMRI paradigm. Inclusion criteria met: I8 (healthy control group reported separately), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates reported). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (not a task-based fMRI study), I6 (no reappraisal strategy/instruction—used self-recalled sadness induction), I7 (stimuli were self-generated autobiographical recall, not static visual images), I9 (no within-task emotion-regulation/reappraisal contrast such as “reappraise > look”). No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) are triggered. Full text appears complete.
